Commentary.Commentary: And that's a wrap for today's game! Pakistan have taken the series, but the excitement isn't over yet. Join us on Sunday, June 1st, at 3 pm GMT for the third and final T20 match. Stay tuned for pre-match buildup and get ready for more action-packed cricket! Cheers!

Salman Agha, the skipper of Pakistan, says that it feels good to win the series, and it was a complete team performance. He adds that they have a strong team with good replacements. He also mentions that they need to strengthen their bowling department. Finally, he says that he's enjoying his role as skipper.

Litton Das, the skipper of Bangladesh, says that Shoriful's injury shifted the momentum against them and they failed with the bat. He adds that they have one more game left and they need to regroup and discuss how to bounce back strongly.

Sahibzada Farhan is the Player of the Match for his knock of 74 runs. He says that he is overwhelmed with emotion, having made a successful comeback and earning Player of the Match. He credits his domestic experience and franchise cricket for teaching him to perform at a high level. Ends by saying that he is now focused on improving more and playing better.
Presentations coming up...

Earlier in the game, Pakistan posted 201 runs, similar to their previous score, thanks to a strong partnership between Sahibzada Farhan and Mohammad Haris. Farhan scored 74, while Hasan Nawaz finished unbeaten on 51, continuing his impressive form. Bangladesh's bowlers restricted Pakistan in the death overs, with Hasan Mahmud and Tanzim Hasan Sakib each taking 2 wickets.

Bangladesh's batting lineup struggled to build momentum, with Tanzid Hasan being the only top order batter to reach double figures. Tanzim Hasan Sakib's late surge, scoring a half-century, was a lone bright spot in an otherwise disappointing innings. Bangladesh were eventually bowled out for 144 in 19 overs.

So, Pakistan seal the series with a convincing 57-run victory over Bangladesh in Lahore, dominating the match with another strong batting display and effective bowling. They scored over 200 runs again and bundled the visitors inside 19 overs. Abrar Ahmed was the pick of the Pakistani bowlers, claiming 3/19 from his four overs, while Faheem Ashraf, Shadab Khan, Saim Ayub, Hasan Ali, Khushdil Shah, and Haris Rauf each chipped in with a wicket.
Shoriful Islam suffered an injury while bowling and will not bat now. So that's the end of the contest and Pakistan seal this series.
